headline: OGCI publishes report on scaling CCS across the Asia-Pacific region
summary: A new Oil and Gas Climate Initiative report, prepared by the Global CCS Institute, examines the policy, regulatory, storage and economic conditions needed to accelerate CCS deployment across Asia-Pacific, with screening-level storage assessments (including Australia's North West Shelf) and a gap analysis calling for greater regulatory alignment and investment.
co2crc_note: APAC-focused CCS scaling report with screening-level storage assessment (incl. Australia's North West Shelf) and a regulatory-gap analysis directly relevant to CO2CRC's regional strategy.
extractor_note: Report/publication item; no financial dimension. Collection partly impaired today (WebFetch egress blocks on several trade-press domains; Outlook newsletters unavailable).

headline: Isometric signs its first China-based carbon-removal projects
summary: Carbon-removal registry Isometric signed its first three China-based CDR developers — DAC firm DeCarbon Tech and biochar developers Tongao Greenchar and Vastwing Energy — to certify projects against its protocols, extending Western CDR-registry standards into China.
co2crc_note: Signals CDR-registry standardisation reaching China's DAC/biochar developers; peripheral to CO2CRC's geological-storage focus.
extractor_note: Radar: story broke ~10 Aug 2026, one calendar day outside the Thu 13 Aug window (which starts 12 Aug).

headline: Cement plants could become net carbon-removal machines, ETH Zurich study finds
summary: Science-press coverage of an ETH Zurich study (Bardow group, Chem Circularity, June 2026) showing calcium-looping direct air capture combined with electrified kilns could cut cement's climate impact by up to 78% by 2050 and turn plants into net CO2 removers.
co2crc_note: Peer-reviewed pathway (calcium-looping DAC + electrified kilns) for turning cement plants into net CO2 removers; long-horizon technology interest.
extractor_note: Radar: science-press writeup (12 Aug) of a June 2026 Chem Circularity study; underlying research out of the daily window.
